elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.1 now reads: "The Company may participate in any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or any other products, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand." Both the participation bar ("shall not participate in any project similar to the Site ... with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar") and the HDI exclusive right in the Company's own "Deerskin" brand are removed, so no non-compete and no field-of-use/brand exclusivity binds Customer. Deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no restriction on Customer exists at all, so there is no scope to narrow to a named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction survives; the original term-only anchor ("during the term of this Agreement") is deleted along with the covenant, leaving nothing that could extend post-term.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no restrictive period because the covenant is removed entirely.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no restriction, Customer's internal development is unrestricted; no carve-out is needed.
Condition does not apply: with no restriction, acquisitions are unconstrained; the narrow Section 6.2 closeout carve-out is no longer load-bearing.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative rewrite of 6.1 eliminates both the project/product participation bar and HDI's exclusive right in the Company's own "Deerskin" brand, which is required because a "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right blocks Customer use of its own brand.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no restriction on Customer remains; they are recorded as met with the condition-inapplicable explanation rather than as omissions.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the two restrictive operative mechanics in Section 6.1 (the participation covenant and the brand exclusivity) and adds no survival tail, procedure, damages category, or obligation outside the NONCOMPETE checklist. The affirmative confirmation is the functional equivalent of deletion and imposes no new requirement on HDI beyond negating the exclusivity that the element requires be removed.

The dropped opening words "Except as provided in Section 6.2" are not a separate cosmetic deletion: the exception existed only to qualify the deleted covenant, and Section 6.2 itself is retained in full, so no favourable Customer language is lost.

Intent is preserved: Section 6.2 (closeout merchandise) and HDI's own covenant in Section 6.3 are untouched and remain internally consistent, since a permissive 6.1 cannot contradict a carve-out from a restriction. No undefined term is created; "Deerskin Products" remains defined in Section 1.1.

Finding status "deviation" is correct on the original text, which failed fallback on scope (open-ended "products substantially similar" and "companies similar to" unnamed retailers) and lacked internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.

Housekeeping only: confirm that Section 6.2 does not open with a "Notwithstanding Section 6.1" style lead-in that would now read oddly; if it does, no substantive change is needed but the lead-in could be conformed.
